olivia: Heads-up: after last kernel-selection tweak, we see host-side p99 decode + tokenization up ~10% on steady-state. Traces point to an extra memcpy in proto parse + smaller batches hitting a slower kernel. Anyone else seeing this?

mike: Yep, noticed on canary this morning. p50 is roughly same, tail worse. CI perf run: p99 from ~120ms -> ~135ms for short sequences.

sasha: Profiled ingress on host-1a: grpc stack spends more time in io_readv and proto_unmarshal after the change. Also seeing more frequent KV-cache misses because chunk boundaries shifted. Snap of perf top:
```
  24.5% io_readv
  18.0% proto_unmarshal
  12.1% memcpy
  10.2% kv_cache_lookup
```

eden: The kernel selector now favors the 'fast-long' path; short sequences fall back to the slower generic kernel. We should update batching/kernel heuristic to consider seq_len distribution before picking kernel.

mike: Quick local test: pin selector to old policy on canary -> p99 returns to baseline. Suggest patch: if seq_len < 128 && batch_size < 8 then prefer 'fast-short' kernel.

sasha: Another datapoint: new stream slicer emits more tiny writes (sub-1kb) which increases syscall overhead. Gateway writev coalescing used to merge into ~8kb writes; now we get many small frames. Could tweak chunker to a min chunk size.

olivia: Plan: 1) revert kernel-selection change on canary, 2) add short-seq heuristic, 3) tweak streaming chunk coalesce to avoid tiny writes, 4) run KV-cache hotkey replay to quantify misses. Who can own 1/2?

mike: I'll own 1 & 2. ETA ~2h to push canary patch and smoke.

sasha: I'll take 3 and run the kvcache hot-shard replay. ETA ~4h.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout canary to 10% (build #4721).

eden: :thumbsup: Logging tasks and filing INF-817 for follow-ups.

olivia: If canary looks good we roll forward. If tail still high we'll bisect the kernel selector commits and loop in @perf-owners.

mike: Adding a short unit test to ensure the selector uses seq_len+batch hints for path decision. Will post PR link when ready.

sasha: Also adding a small harness to simulate small-write pressure for the streaming layer. Should catch regressions earlier.

(especially important: keep an eye on KV cache hitrate and syscall counts per request)
